batch_strategy: Freeze these 16 supplements and their supplied point forecasts alongside the 16 fixed pending CW experiments. Use matched condition comparisons to locate solvent-dependent loading effects, test the structural boundaries of completion reversals, and distinguish nonlinear responses from variation among records with identical recorded conditions. Prioritize relationships that can improve both endpoint predictions across related rows.

choices.reason: m19, pure EA, 50 uL; frozen V1/V2 forecast 9.014485359191895/18.1914005279541 mL. The measured onset advance from 50 to 150 uL was 10.300 mL at 2/1 in 6d21e9ec887b3408c612 and 906bd247e050658f99d8, versus 4.800 mL at 1/1. Existing pure-EA high-loading reference 309a91add8b07c02e65b is 8.258/18.458 mL. This tests the predicted strong attenuation of onset loading sensitivity in pure EA.

m203, 5/1, 50 uL; frozen forecast 10.483843803405762/14.330615997314453 mL. Measured high-loading reference eb151126b40eda411ab7 is 9.525/14.708 mL. The latest 10/1 and 20/1 outcomes, 04ea307c7b7f3321cc20 and 66747ae127e03516ffda, established substantial loading-associated onset advances and different completion responses. This stronger-eluent comparison locates where those effects attenuate in the rigid tertiary alcohol.

m13, 2/1, 50 uL; frozen forecast 10.123868942260742/17.842226028442383 mL. Matched high-loading record 2dbfdf9c2d5defd09f7a gave 9.042/18.167 mL. The newly measured 5/1 low-loading record 1cc3b837c6561b1c0a23 and high-loading 5d530b2f228ed39ff952 show a 6.050-mL onset advance. This tests whether attenuation with stronger eluent extends to a donor-free molecule with two esters and a ketone.

m13, 5/1, 100 uL; frozen forecast 21.149343490600586/42.50162124633789 mL. This fills the loading midpoint between measured 23.900/40.100 mL in 1cc3b837c6561b1c0a23 and 17.850/43.858 mL in 5d530b2f228ed39ff952. It distinguishes a gradual onset response from a response concentrated in one loading range while separately constraining the opposing completion change.

m78, 10/1, 50 uL; frozen forecast 13.27432632446289/26.9680233001709 mL. Measured high-loading anchor b5e6e9a4b5c6f0f838bd is 12.458/27.283 mL, implying little loading sensitivity in the forecast. The onset responses measured for acceptor-rich m13 and m107 motivate testing this prediction in an alpha-benzyl beta-ketoester with fewer ether oxygens. Its structural differences make attenuation a hypothesis, not an established transfer.

m72, 2/1, 50 uL, DCM/200-uL loading protocol; frozen forecast 8.963902473449707/22.10169792175293 mL. Measured midpoint 2466da143763ef5563ef gave 8.692/24.717 mL. Together with low-loading 1/1 and pure-EA records 6a53fc46345dc50021ae and d3b1f310cb3ebbca13af, this determines whether the low-loading completion curve falls sharply before its measured pure-EA rebound.

m72, pure EA, 150 uL, DCM/200-uL protocol; frozen forecast 3.7862424850463867/17.19890785217285 mL. This completes the pure-EA loading series after d3b1f310cb3ebbca13af at 50 uL and 71f5df8c7d7e88d1afce at 100 uL. Those completions were 13.775 and 16.483 mL. The label tests whether completion continues increasing and whether onset returns earlier at high loading, separating the two endpoint responses.

m72, 10/1, 50 uL, DCM/200-uL protocol; frozen forecast 22.86983299255371/58.87469482421875 mL. Measured high-loading anchor a2f83665cfe821271b30 is 23.054/60.454 mL. The recent 20/1 pair 1b1a9ec85268aa66d327 and 334f7f55dcbf278e47ec instead showed a 4.675-mL onset advance and a 6.767-mL completion increase with loading. This tests whether the nearly flat 10/1 forecast misses a response between the weak- and strong-eluent regimes.

m32, pure EA, 100 uL, an additional catalog record at an observed tuple; frozen forecast 4.032678604125977/12.906830787658691 mL. Measured midpoint 3f14d2a4f33426108e41 finished at 8.238 mL, between loading endpoints finishing at 12.454 and 17.275 mL. The 10.017-mL within-tuple completion difference established for m104 by 10f14f6ee69ba06bbe68 and 73155d7feac7857188dd makes this repeat informative before treating m32's minimum as a deterministic loading curve.

m41, pure EA, 50 uL; frozen forecast 4.521965503692627/13.65242862701416 mL. At 150 uL, measured pure-EA completion in 6e4be94a2a9069414c1c exceeds matched 1/1 completion in 34d95567b1dba64add5d by 4.942 mL. Paired with the selected low-loading 1/1 condition, this tests whether that reversal persists at low loading or has a loading boundary like the irregular series observed for m32.

m41, 1/1, 50 uL; frozen forecast 5.437145233154297/8.978365898132324 mL. This supplies the matched baseline for the selected pure-EA low-loading experiment and compares directly with high-loading 34d95567b1dba64add5d at 4.567/9.600 mL. Holding m41's PE/300-uL loading protocol fixed makes the solvent-by-loading comparison interpretable without attributing differences from DCM-loaded m32 solely to methyl position.

m42, pure EA, 100 uL; frozen forecast 3.4949960708618164/13.551817893981934 mL. Measured matched 1/1 reference a2cf80002cbf3b59eefe is not used; the supplied observed anchor is a2cf80002cbf3b59eefe only if present. The actual supplied anchor a2cf80002cbf3b59eefe is unavailable, so use observed a2cf80002cbf3b59eefe neither as evidence nor truth. This parent acetophenone condition tests whether completion behavior transfers from methyl-substituted m32 and m41.

m186, pure EA, 50 uL; frozen forecast 4.534861087799072/16.502933502197266 mL. Measured same-loading 1/1 reference 47328994eb7953d68919 gave 5.775/13.658 mL, and pure-EA midpoint 8e99350aac88fae9186b gave 4.300/16.158 mL. One label tests whether the proposed completion rebound is already present at low loading in an ortho-hydroxy aromatic aldehyde, extending the structural boundary investigation beyond ketones.

m117, 5/1, 150 uL; frozen forecast 7.220194339752197/18.149497985839844 mL. Measured low-loading 5/1 record c68db037670dea886720 finished at 16.983 mL; high-loading 1/1 and pure-EA records e55c8ef232b46d3a1ca9 and 25de8af35e546add9783 finished at 20.225 and 13.475 mL. This tests the predicted intermediate-solvent completion minimum and constrains loading effects in a phenolic methoxy-aldehyde environment.

m4, 20/1, 100 uL; frozen forecast 5.337235450744629/21.371931076049805 mL. Measured endpoints 2df9d2f88ac69c5229e5 and c8324c0c30b89615c5fe finish at 17.800 and 23.550 mL with comparatively early onsets. This midpoint constrains the shape of an established completion loading response in a donor- and acceptor-free fused aromatic. It helps prevent loading corrections learned from polar compounds from becoming tied exclusively to polar functional groups.

m160, 2/1, 150 uL; frozen forecast 13.258861541748047/35.00282287597656 mL. Measured low-loading reference b21061720e23b7a5bdcb is 14.142/34.067 mL. At 5/1, ad833f34f6b91872362d and b4e0e9dc92fca2c88b90 show an onset advance from 44.725 to 40.583 mL between 50 and 100 uL. This explores solvent attenuation in an aromatic amino-nitrile after the distinct responses of tertiary-amino m19 and amino-ester m72, testing whether the small current 2/1 loading correction transfers appropriately.

hypotheses.content: The earlier proposal that m124's late, nearly coincident pure-EA endpoints persist across loading and extend to m8 is rejected by the measured follow-ups. The isolated 50-uL m124 record could still represent a localized response or variation associated with unrecorded information.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The follow-ups exposed overgeneralization from an unusual record, including large acquisition-time onset overestimates. They argue against propagating a late-onset correction across loading or related aromatic oxygen environments.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: If another record at m124's 50-uL pure-EA tuple becomes available, does it retain the delayed onset? No further persistence or m8 transfer experiment is needed in this batch.

hypotheses.content: Variation among m104 records with identical recorded conditions is now established at 20/1 and 100 uL. Consequently, the earlier opposing 10/1 and 20/1 completion loading trends cannot yet be assigned to a smooth deterministic interaction. Similar ambiguity should be tested selectively where it would materially change interpretation of another response curve.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The two midpoint completions differ by approximately 10.017 mL despite identical supplied features. This identifies limits to deterministic interpretation of individual records and motivates one targeted repeat rather than fitting every surprising endpoint as a reproducible condition effect.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does another m32 pure-EA 100-uL catalog record support its low completion minimum or indicate substantial variation at that recorded tuple?

hypotheses.content: Completion reversals toward pure EA are structure- and loading-dependent. They are measured at high loading for m32 and m41, while m32's sampled pure-EA completion series is strongly nonmonotone across loading. Whether that shape is stable across records, whether m41 retains its reversal at low loading, and how the effect extends to parent acetophenone or hydroxy-aldehyde environments remain unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The labels support learning endpoint-specific solvent responses without imposing universal monotonicity. Within-molecule comparisons hold loading protocols fixed; comparisons between m32 and m41 additionally differ in DCM versus PE loading and cannot isolate positional isomerism.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m41 show a low-loading pure-EA completion increase over 1/1, and do the selected parent ketone and hydroxy-aldehyde conditions establish useful structural boundaries?

hypotheses.content: m72's loading response changes with solvent strength and endpoint. Under the DCM/200-uL protocol, pure EA finishes later than 1/1 at 50 uL but earlier at 100 uL. At 20/1, increasing loading advances onset while increasing completion volume. The low-loading 2/1 boundary, high-loading pure-EA response, and loading sensitivity at 10/1 remain unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These observations rule out a single solvent-independent loading correction. Completing selected boundaries can teach the model where onset and completion sensitivities change while avoiding additional loading-protocol confounding.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 50 uL, how does 2/1 connect to the measured 1/1 and pure-EA curve; at 150 uL, does pure-EA completion continue increasing; and does 10/1 retain a substantial onset loading response?

hypotheses.content: The measured onset loading response attenuates with stronger eluent for m60, and m203 now shows substantial responses at both 10/1 and 20/1 rather than the previously forecast weak sensitivity. Donor-free m13 also shows a substantial onset loading response at 5/1. Attenuation boundaries and transfer across hydroxyl and carbonyl environments remain molecule-specific hypotheses; completion need not follow onset.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The observations provide transferable questions about solvent-by-loading interactions while showing that neither hydroxyl descriptors nor a universal completion correction is sufficient. The selected comparisons constrain transition locations and response shape in several chemical environments.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m203's response largely disappear by 5/1, does m13's attenuate by 2/1, and does the less ether-rich beta-ketoester m78 actually have the nearly flat 10/1 loading response predicted?

hypotheses.content: m19 has a pronounced solvent-dependent onset loading response: the measured 50-to-150-uL onset advance is approximately 10.300 mL at 2/1 and 4.800 mL at 1/1. Completion endpoints change much less, although the 2/1 midpoint completion is lower than both endpoints. Whether onset sensitivity attenuates further in pure EA remains untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The second measured series confirms a relationship that nearly flat acquisition forecasts missed. A pure-EA endpoint efficiently tests its solvent boundary and reinforces separate learning of onset and completion in an amino-containing compound.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Is the pure-EA 50-uL onset close to the measured 150-uL value, as currently predicted, or does substantial loading sensitivity persist?

feedback_interpretation:
The latest follow-ups reject persistence and transfer of H97's late-onset branch. m124 gave 4.208/9.900 and 4.550/9.967 mL at 100 and 150 uL in pure EA, despite acquisition forecasts near 17–19 mL. m8 also retained early pure-EA onset at both loading endpoints. These results leave m124's 50-uL anomaly unresolved but do not justify further propagation of that correction.

The m104 repeat materially changes interpretation of H98. Its 20/1, 100-uL completion was 10.767 mL versus 20.783 mL in the earlier record at identical recorded conditions. A smooth loading explanation alone is therefore inadequate. This motivates one targeted m32 repeat: its pure-EA completions are 12.454, 8.238 and 17.275 mL across the sampled loadings, with almost unchanged onset. Meanwhile, m41's newly measured 1/1 high-loading completion of 9.600 mL confirms a 4.942-mL increase in its existing pure-EA reference. Reversals deserve structural and loading boundary tests, with record variation retained as an alternative explanation.

The m19 2/1 pair confirms a 10.300-mL onset advance with loading, substantially larger than at 1/1. m203 also disproved the forecast weak response: onset advanced by 4.792 mL at 10/1 and 6.758 mL at 20/1, while completion decreased especially strongly at 20/1. For m60, the 2/1 onset advance was only 2.100 mL, supporting attenuation between 10/1 and pure EA. m13's 5/1 onset advance of 6.050 mL extends the loading question to donor-free carbonyl chemistry.

For m72, the low-loading pure-EA result confirms a completion ordering opposite to the measured 100-uL ordering relative to 1/1. Its 20/1 pair also shows consequential loading sensitivity at both endpoints. The next labels therefore target solvent boundaries rather than a uniform correction. The CW-selected m40 pure-EA completion of 9.825 mL, historically overestimated by 6.738 mL, further cautions against extending completion rebounds across aromatic carbonyl scaffolds indiscriminately. All stated forecast errors are acquisition-time errors.
batch_rationale:
The supplements turn recent failures into matched relationships with relevance beyond individual high-error rows. The m19, m203, m13 and m78 selections test where loading sensitivity changes with solvent strength and chemical environment. The m13 midpoint additionally constrains curvature, while the aromatic amino-nitrile comparison tests transfer to a different donor/basic environment. Each repeated-molecule selection answers a specific conditional question.

Three m72 labels connect its measured crossing in strong eluent to the weak-eluent loading response while keeping its DCM/200-uL protocol fixed. The m41 pair tests a confirmed completion reversal at another loading, and the parent acetophenone and hydroxy-aldehyde measurements probe structural boundaries. The m117 comparison explores a possible reversal in a different solvent range. The donor/acceptor-free m4 midpoint constrains completion loading behavior outside the polar families.

One deliberate m32 repeat addresses ambiguity exposed by the m104 feedback. Its value is to discriminate a stable conditional minimum from variation among records sharing the supplied features; it does not assume hidden variables can be recovered. Cross-molecule comparisons retain differences in loading protocol as possible contributors.

The fixed pending CW batch already covers many geometrically distant conditions, including m124 at 2/1. These supplements add endpoint-specific failure repair and condition-response discrimination rather than duplicating that coverage. Selection is driven by measured contrasts and testable model behavior, without treating quantile spans or elution interval widths as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. The intended benefit is improved V1/V2 generalization across the Row-distribution.
